method: Protein: L = 10th percentile, T = 90th percentile of zscore pooled across all detected=True rows (one global pair, not per-gene). Dependency: L = 10th percentile, T = 90th percentile of -dependency_score ('dependency strength'), per gene, gated at N>=30 lines/gene. Copy number: L = 10th percentile, T = 90th percentile of the continuous copy_number value, per gene, same N>=30 gate. r_default = 1 (Derringer & Suich linear desirability, matching the RNA calibration). P5 note: protein's zscore is now detection-floor imputed upstream in preprocessing/impute.py -- this calibration still filters on detected==True exactly as it always did, so the imputed floor value is correctly excluded from the percentile.
gene_filter: kept genes where T > L (any discrimination), same rule as the RNA calibration
no_per_lineage_override: Unlike RNA, none of these three layers has a per-lineage override -- RNA's own in-sample per-lineage override is a deliberate one-layer investment, not yet extended here. Documented simplification, not a silent gap.
